applicability_policy: Every evidence item has one direct applicability reference wholly within Genesis 10 or 11. Genesis 12:2, Genesis 1:28, Genesis 9, Job, ancient comparanda, and later reception appear only in descriptive prose/source locators, never as evidence scripture_references.

accepted.basis: All 29 items passed schema/provenance/applicability review, were directly anchored within Genesis 10–11, and every one was present in the corresponding chapter synthesis.

rejected.claim: Nimrod equals Gilgamesh, Sargon, Naram-Sin, Tukulti-Ninurta, or Marduk as established fact.
rejected.reason: No adequate evidence establishes any such identity.

rejected.claim: The Tower of Babel has been found.
rejected.reason: Archaeology supports Mesopotamian ziggurat comparison, not discovery of the narrated tower.
This projects modern race theory into ancient ethnographic and genealogical language; Genesis 9 names Canaan in the oracle.

rejected.claim: Peleg’s “earth was divided” documents continental drift.
rejected.reason: The text does not supply geological evidence for plate tectonics.

rejected.claim: Genesis 11 is a technical scientific history of every human language.
rejected.reason: The narrative functions as literary/theological etiology and does not provide a technical history of all languages.

unresolved: The exact historical referents of Magog and Tiras, and the precise location meant by Tarshish.
The location of Calneh and the grammatical subject in the Asshur/Nineveh city notice.
The exact historical identity of Nimrod and the nuance of lifnei YHWH.
The precise location intended by Ur of the Chaldeans and the historical setting of the itinerary.
The chronology and compositional relationship between the Table of Nations and Babel episode.

withheld.claim: Nimrod is securely identifiable as a named Mesopotamian ruler.
withheld.reason: The historical identification does not meet the evidence threshold; Levin is retained only as a scholarly proposal.

withheld.claim: A specific excavated ziggurat is proven to be the Genesis tower.
withheld.reason: Etemenanki is a bounded comparator; the biblical text names no excavated structure.

withheld.claim: The precise locations of Tarshish, Magog, Tiras, or Calneh are established.
withheld.reason: The ancient identifications remain disputed or unknown.

withheld.claim: Ur of the Chaldeans is identified with certainty, or Abraham’s house has been excavated.
withheld.reason: Southern Ur is commonly favored, but exact identification and patriarchal attribution remain unproven.

coverage_expectation: Recalculate chapter classifications using the G0 coverage approach after staging and after apply. Do not force GOOD.
identity_and_confidence_policy: Use SECURE_OR_WIDELY_ACCEPTED / PROBABLE / DISPUTED / UNKNOWN labels for ethnogeographic identifications. No modern nationalist or racial identifications.

proposed_object.architecture: one isolated reusable evidence container; no structured additions to legacy fallback objects and no reciprocal relationships

source_disposition_policy.accepted: Supported passage-specific items with local source records
source_disposition_policy.rejected: Nimrod equals named king as established; Tower of Babel found; modern racial reading; Peleg continental drift; Genesis provides technical scientific history of all languages; archaeological proof of Abraham’s house
source_disposition_policy.unresolved: Ur of the Chaldeans exact identification and several ethnonyms
source_disposition_policy.withheld: Claims with inadequate evidence, including exact Tarshish/Magog/Tiras or Calneh locations, a proven historical Nimrod identity, exact Genesis tower identification, and exact date of composition

source_dispositions.notes: All included sources are used for bounded, source-backed claims. Interpretive conclusions and disputed identifications are qualified in the evidence items.

source_owner_invariant: 0 existing historical source-owner rows changed; G3 source records local to the new object; reuse shared works by local alias.
